newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Investors seen paying top price for Portugal's EDP.
newsitem.headline: Investors seen paying top price for Portugal's EDP.

text.p: Investors look set to pay near the maximum 2,250 escudos per share in the privatisation of EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, banking sources said as subscriptions closed on Thursday.
"The orders...were placed at best or at the top price," said one banking source close to the sale, of bids lodged by institutional investors.
The Socialist government set a range of 1,750-2,250 escudos per share for the sale of 30 percent of EDP in what will be the largest privatisation yet carried out in Portugal.
The final price will be fixed after the stock market closes on Monday, June 16, on the basis of bids made by institutional investors.
The sale of the 180 million shares, which will earn the government some 400 billion escudos, is known to have been many times oversubscribed.
"Most of the orders from the institutions did not even bother to put a price," said another banking source, meaning they would pay whatever price was set.
Some 100 million shares, equal to a little over 60 percent, will be offered to the general public, with company employees, emigrants and small investors getting a slight discount.
The remainder is being sold directly to institutional investors -- banks, pension funds and companies.
Banking sources said that the demand had been so heavy from the public that investors were likely to end up with as few as 2.5 shares for every 100 sought.
But even if the stock is sold at the top of the range, most analysts see room for a significant price appreciation once it trades on the market.
"A lot of people are going to end up not getting all the stock that they want," said one banking source involved in the sale.

"It is virtually obligatory for domestic investment funds to have a slice of EDP and if they do not get the amounts they want at the privatisation, they will have to buy on the open market, pushing up the price," he added.
The same went for foreign investors, the source said.
Shares in Portugal Telecom have virtually doubled in price since the second phase of its heavily oversubscribed privatisation a year ago.
